chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi. He said: I said to Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him):
Which qualities are most beautiful in a person? He said: Dignity without intimidation, generosity without seeking recompense, and preoccupation with something other than the enjoyments of this world.
ai.seo_question: What are the most beautiful qualities a person can have according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) was asked by his companion Ahmad al-Halabi about the finest qualities a person can possess. The Imam identified three traits that together form a portrait of noble character: composed dignity that does not intimidate others, selfless generosity that expects nothing in return, and a purposeful life oriented away from worldly materialism. This teaching was delivered in a private scholarly setting, reflecting the Imam's method of moral instruction through concise, memorable maxims.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Al-Haytham b. Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to us from `Abd al-`Aziz b. `Umar from Ahmad b. `Umar al-Halabi. He said: I said to Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as):
What characteristics are most beautiful for a person? He said: Piety without sanctimoniousness, forgiveness without seeking recompense, and industriousness without seeking the frills of this world.
